# <span style="color: black;">**PROJECT DESCRIPTION**</span>

\

The analysis was performed on the following samples:\

```{r table_meta, echo=FALSE}
library("reactable")
library("htmltools")

meta <- read.csv(params$samples_meta)

reactable(
  meta[1:4],
  resizable = TRUE,
  #filterable = TRUE,
  searchable = TRUE,
  highlight = TRUE,
  outlined = TRUE,
  bordered = TRUE,
  striped = TRUE,
  compact = TRUE,
  showSortIcon = TRUE,
  showSortable = TRUE,
  # Aggiungi uno stile generale per colorare l'intestazione
  theme = reactableTheme(
    headerStyle = list(
      backgroundColor = "deepskyblue", # Sfondo azzurro
      color = "black",            # Testo nero
      fontWeight = "bold"         # Testo in grassetto
      # be careful that it doesn't work with some colors
    )
  )
)

```



\

## <span style="color: black;">**RESULTS**</span>

A series of quality control (QC) filters and checks was applied to each sample to evaluate data integrity. 
After individual sample analysis, the samples were first merged to assess for the presence of potential batch effects and then integrated. Integration was performed using Harmony procedure to minimize batch effects and highlight meaningful biological differences. The merged and integrated datasets were then characterized to produce unbiased clustering across all samples, UMAP visualizations and cluster-specific marker identification.
\
\

## <span style="color: black;">**Integration**</span>

The Seurat objects belonging to each sample were then put together to perform 
the integration step.\
The total number of cells used for the integration analysis was 48,865 cells.
\
The samples were integrated using Harmony, after which the integrated dataset was processed performing PCA and UMAP as dimensional reduction algorithms and applying the SNN clustering to identify distinct cell populations.\
\


## <span style="color: black;">**Clustering**</span>

\

The clustering was performed using `r params$nPCs` nPCs with the following resolutions: `r params$resolutions`. \
UMAPs were generated for each resolution. \

\

```{r umap-res-loop, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
out <- NULL

out <- c(out, "## UMAPs by resolution {.tabset}", "")

for (res in params$resolutions) {
  res_str <- as.character(res)
  out <- c(out, knitr::knit_child(
    text = c(
      sprintf("### Resolution %s", res_str),
      "",
      "```{r echo=FALSE, out.width='100%', fig.align='center'}",
      sprintf("knitr::include_graphics(paste0(params$out_location_seurat, 'plot/UMAPs/dim_integrated_cluster_RES%s_%s.png'))", res_str, params$cellbender_tag),
      "```",
      ""
    ),
    quiet = TRUE
  ))
}

out <- c(out, "## {- .leave-tabset}", "")

cat(paste(out, collapse = "\n"))
```

## <span style="color: black;">**Cluster Markers**</span>

\

The The **`r params$report_resolution` resolution** was selected as the final clustering resolution, and all downstream analyses were performed based on this clustering.
\
\
The differential gene expression analysis was performed among all clusters on the integrated object with the Seurat function `FindAllMarkers`.\
This one performs a Wilcoxon test to identify gene markers for each cluster compared to all other clusters. The expression for a given gene among cells in a given cluster is compared against the expression of that gene among cells in all other clusters. In the output, pct.1 is the percentage of cells in the cluster where the gene is detected, while pct.2 is the percentage of cells on average in all the other clusters where the gene is detected. A gene to be considered as an IDEAL cluster marker is expected to be expressed exclusively in that cluster and silenced in all others and thus pct.1 will be more towards 1 and pct.2 towards 0.
\

The top 5 specific markers for each cluster were represented in both a Dotplot and a Heatmap:
\
\
```{r TopMA, echo = FALSE, out.width='100%', fig.align='center', fig.cap='Top 5 specific markers for each cluster'}
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(params$out_location_seurat,
                                 "plot/Dotplot_RNA_snn_res.", params$report_resolution, ".png"))

```
\

## <span style="color: black;">**Annotation of Clusters**</span>

\

Cell type annotation was performed using **[CyteType](https://cytetype.nygen.io)** and SingleR.
CyteType is an AI-powered automated annotation platform developed by Nygen Analytics.

CyteType integrates cluster-specific marker genes (identified by `FindAllMarkers`) with UMAP coordinates and leverages large language models trained on curated single-cell atlases to assign biologically meaningful cell type labels to each cluster. The platform returns cluster-level annotations with confidence scores and supporting marker evidence, and provides an interactive web-based visualization for exploring results.

\

```{r cytetype-link, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cytetype_info <- jsonlite::fromJSON(params$cytetype_job_id_file)
url <- cytetype_info$report_url
if (!is.null(url) && nzchar(url)) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "&#x1F517; **[Click here to explore the CyteType interactive annotation results](%s)**",
    url
  ))
} else {
  cat("_CyteType annotation URL not available._")
}
```

\
\

# <span style="color: black;">**SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIALS**</span>

## <span style="color: black;">**Quality Control**</span>

\
Sequenced libraries were mapped to the custom reference genome (`r params$genome`) using CellRanger v10 (10x Genomics). A first step of sequencing quality control was made on all files coming from the different samples after collecting them to obtain fastQC files of the sequencing.

1. [FastQC](https://www.bioinformatics.babraham.ac.uk/projects/fastqc/) v0.11.9 (latest v0.12.0): It gives us an idea of the quality of the R2 reads, containing transcripts.

2. [Cellranger](https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/latest) count (v10.0): It was used to select barcodes containing live/high quality cells with a high amount of transcripts.

All these results with their QC logs and plots were collected and presented using [MultiQC](https://multiqc.info/) v1.21 (latest 1.25.1, not tested yet) plots and the html collection of data obtained by Cellranger count function.

 The quality metrics are available by downloading the MultiQC report here:
\
```{r QC_report, echo=FALSE, warning=F, message = FALSE}
xfun::embed_file("../results/multiQC/merged/multiqc_report.html",
                 text = "Download the MultiQC report")
```
\

## <span style="color: black;">**Doublets detection**</span>

\

[scDblFinder](https://plger.github.io/scDblFinder/) was used to detect doublets in the scRNAseq data. Doublets occur when two or more cells are mistakenly captured in the same droplet during the sequencing process, leading to mixed or incorrect transcriptomic profiles for a single cell. In our standard pipeline doublets are just highlighted but not removed.

\
```{r Doublets, echo = FALSE, out.width='100%', fig.align='center', fig.cap='UMAPs showing the doublets presence', fig.show = 'hold'}
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(params$out_location_seurat, "plot/UMAPs/dim_scDblFinder.score_", params$cellbender_tag, ".png"))
```
\

```{r Doublets_download, echo = FALSE}
xfun::embed_file(paste0(params$out_location_seurat, "plot/UMAPs/dim_scDblFinder.score_", params$cellbender_tag, ".pdf"),
                 text = "Download the UMAP with doublets")
```
\

## <span style="color: black;">**Merged Dataset Analysis**</span>

In addition to the integrated dataset analyses presented in this report, we also provide an analysis based on the merged (non-integrated) dataset. This analysis preserves the original expression values of each sample without batch correction and may be useful for assessing sample-specific features and comparing results with the integrated dataset.
